# ECON 0100 | Homework E3 | Monopoly

*Homework is a tool to highlight what you don’t yet understand. Grading is for completion, so there are no additional points for turning in perfect answers you don’t fully understand. Use your areas of confusion to guide your study. Work in a group and ask others for help.*

## Q1 | The History of the Broomstick Market

In the early days of the broomstick market, CloudSweep was the first maker of the standard broom, developing a proprietary method for autolocomotion. Since they were the only maker, they were the only seller in the market. As in Homework E1, it has high fixed costs, $FC=1000$ coins per week, and a constant marginal cost, $MC = 15$ coins per unit. As the only seller it faces the whole market’s demand and charges the same price for every broom. Demand and marginal revenue are:

$$
D: P = 135 - Q \qquad\qquad MR = 135 - 2Q
$$

where $Q$ is the number of brooms it makes in a week. Each graph shows demand and marginal cost.

:::: {.columns gutter=0.5em}

::: {.column width=60%}

a\) Graph marginal revenue ($MR$).\
b\) Find and graph the profit-maximizing quantity ($Q^*$).\
c\) Find and graph the price that sells that quantity ($P^*$).\
d\) Find CloudSweep’s maximized profit.\
e\) Find and graph the socially efficient quantity.\
f\) Find and shade the deadweight loss.

:::

## Q2 | A Monopoly on Brooms

As technological secrets for manufacturing broomsticks began disseminating among the wizarding world, many broomstick makers began producing broomsticks with identical handling and acceleration characteristics to CouldSweep’s brooms. Today, few if any new broomstick makers had opened.

Using a few graphs to illustrate your answer, tell the story of the evolution of the broomstick market from it’s inception to the present. Be sure to finish in a long run equilibrium.
